_about: The order in which Liebermann prints the clauses of law codes whose order is not simply numerical (Alfred keeps Thorpe’s and Schmid’s numbers out of order; Epilog, Rubriken and the like are labels, not numbers). tools/laws-from-database.py keeps these codes in this order and never sorts them by number, and warns if a rebuild comes out in a different order. law.html and lawcode.html show the notes: 'notes' on a clause's page, 'codeNotes' in the whole-code views just before the clause named in 'before'.

Af.29: Liebermann’s numbers here are not in numerical order: he keeps Thorpe’s and Schmid’s numbering, but prints the clauses in the order of the manuscripts (Gesetze I, p. 64, n. *).

Af.text: From here to 28, Liebermann’s numbers are not in numerical order: 25,1 is followed by 29–31,1 and then 26–28. He keeps Thorpe’s and Schmid’s numbering, but prints the clauses in the order of the manuscripts (Gesetze I, p. 64, n. *). In H, 25–25,1 stand after 31,1.
